clue.text: Expert turning in best part of shoe

indicators.note: in puts the turned expert inside the word for best

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks

indicators.note: turning tells us to read the word for expert backwards

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A specialist spins round inside the finest part of a shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' makes ECA from ACE, and 'in' sets it inside TOP.
explanation.definitionFit: The reinforced cover over the front of a boot is a standard component of footwear.

clue.text: Nothing put on will encapsulate English theatre

parts.note: O, the zero shape, is nothing

indicators.note: will encapsulate means the word for put on wraps around the English abbreviation

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: Something that dresses up as nothing will contain Englishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will encapsulate' puts E inside DON, after O for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is a name used for a picture house or concert hall, after the ancient Greek building for music.

clue.text: Meet people where roads meet, not quite running behindhand

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter of the word for a road junction is dropped

parts.note: a circus, like Oxford Circus, is a junction where several roads meet
running behind schedule is being late

explanation.surface: Someone networking at a junction finds they are behind time.
explanation.walkthrough: In British towns a 'circus' is a round junction (Piccadilly Circus); 'not quite' cuts it to CIRCU, then LATE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To mingle with guests at a party, moving from one to another, is to go around the room.

clue.text: Recipient of surgery will lose one, that's clear

indicators.note: will lose means a letter is taken out of the word for the surgery recipient

parts.note: a patient is the one who receives surgery
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone under the knife is told they will lose a body part, and that's obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent can mean obvious or evident, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: Unhappy girl following father in US city

indicators.note: following means the sad girl comes after the word for father

parts.note: pa is an informal name for father
unhappy means sad
Ena is a girl's name much used in crosswords

explanation.surface: A miserable girl trails behind her dad in an American town.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasadena is a city in California, home of the Rose Bowl.

clue.text: Small ads have limited impact for one's own possessions

indicators.note: limited means the word for small ads is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: the personals are the small personal advertisements in a newspaper
effects means impact, as in the effects of a storm

explanation.surface: Classified adverts don't make much of a splash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims PERSONALS to PERSONAL; 'have' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's belongings, such as clothes and jewellery, are their private things.

clue.text: People generally accepting British for cold calm attitude

indicators.note: accepting British for cold means B takes the place of C in the word for people generally

parts.note: society is people in general
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
British gives BR

explanation.surface: The public welcomes Britain's chilly, composed manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting British for cold' swaps C for B in SOCIETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobriety is soberness, a serious and restrained state of mind.

clue.text: Prevent one coming out with a right

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman coming out into society

explanation.surface: A girl making her debut comes out with an entitlement.
explanation.walkthrough: A debutante's first formal social season is called her 'coming out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar someone is to exclude or ban them, stopping them from doing something.

clue.text: Lost again, drifting, thinking of the past

indicators.note: drifting suggests the letters wander out of their order

explanation.surface: A traveller lost once more, adrift and recalling old times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' rearranges the nine letters of LOST AGAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a wistful longing for former times.

clue.text: Provoker of lust and unusually hot breath? That's about right

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the letter for right
unusually shows the letters of hot breath are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: Someone exciting desire with strangely hot breath; that's about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges HOT BREATH to HEATTHROB, and 'about' wraps that round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamboat celebrity who makes fans swoon stirs desire.

clue.text: Naval officer's new cry returned

indicators.note: returned means the word for cry is turned back

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: A sailor in charge lets out a fresh wail again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns SOB into BOS, before N.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosn is a short spelling of boatswain, the ship's petty officer in charge of rigging and deck crew.

clue.text: Badly undone after much circulated suggestive comment

indicators.note: after puts the scrambled letters behind the word for popular

parts.note: in means fashionable, much talked about

indicators.note: badly suggests the word undone is put together wrongly

explanation.surface: Something badly undone after being widely passed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges UNDONE to NUENDO, placed 'after' IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Innuendo is a sly hint, often risqué, that implies more than it says.

clue.text: I note staff limiting a depredation

indicators.note: limiting means the staff surrounds the letter a

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: I notice a stick holding back a raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' encloses A in ROD, after I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is a hostile raid into territory, a plundering incursion.

clue.text: Blood constituents will be available in France

explanation.surface: Plasma parts are on sale across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: SERA is the plural of serum and also the French for 'will be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Serums are the clear fluid parts of blood; in French future tense, il sera means he will be.

clue.text: Protocol quite wrong when used in core of letter

indicators.note: used in means the jumbled letters are placed inside the core
core of takes the inner letters of the word letter
wrong suggests the letters of quite are in a faulty order

explanation.surface: Etiquette rules broken when used in the heart of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core of' gives ETTE from LETTER; 'wrong' turns QUITE into TIQUE, 'used in' that core after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette is the code of correct manners, as diplomatic protocol is formal rules of conduct.

clue.text: Superman's relationship with Kent?

parts.note: Clark Kent is the mild reporter identity of the comic-book hero, so the two are one person's other self

explanation.surface: A question about how the Man of Steel gets on with a county or a person.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent looks like the English county, but it is Clark Kent, Superman's everyday identity.
explanation.definitionFit: A second self or secret identity is a person's other persona.

clue.text: Rogue soldiers investigate, holding other soldiers up

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: holding means the word for investigate surrounds the other soldiers

parts.note: to probe is to investigate

indicators.note: up in a down clue tells us to read the other soldiers bottom to top

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, are other soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops look into a scoundrel while keeping another unit raised.
explanation.walkthrough: RE (Royal Engineers) and TA (Territorial Army) are British army units; 'up' makes AT, which PROBE is 'holding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled scoundrel.

clue.text: Wanton harlot I love? Her and many others!

definitions.text: Wanton harlot I love? Her and many others!

indicators.note: wanton means unruly, so the following letters run wild

parts.note: O, a zero score in tennis, is love

explanation.surface: A man boasts of loving a loose woman and plenty more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanton' rearranges HARLOT I into LOTHARI, then O for love; the whole clue describes such a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, named after a rake in an 18th-century play.

clue.text: Book about anger's annoying

indicators.note: about means the word for book goes around the other piece

parts.note: a tome is a large book
ire is anger, and the 's adds the S

explanation.surface: A volume about rage is irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts IRES inside TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious and irritating wears you out.

clue.text: Vegetable product finally used as fuel

definitions.text: Vegetable product finally used as fuel

parts.note: a pea is a vegetable

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of the word product

explanation.surface: Some plant matter ends up burning in the grate.
explanation.walkthrough: PEA plus the last letter of 'product'; the whole clue describes the decayed plant matter dug and burnt.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is decomposed bog vegetation, cut and dried for burning.

clue.text: Stand the result of taking drug overdose?

parts.note: a trip is a hallucinatory experience after taking a drug

explanation.surface: The aftermath of taking a drug overdose asks a question.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripod is a three-legged support for a camera.

clue.text: Race not finished? Cry of suspense — and cheer!

indicators.note: not finished means the last letter of the word for race is cut

parts.note: to hurry is to race
ah is a cry of anticipation

explanation.surface: An unfinished race brings a tense gasp and applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not finished' cuts HURRY to HURR, then AH.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of joy or approval is a hooray.

clue.text: Struggles to comprehend, missing first element of what one learns?

indicators.note: missing first element means the opening letter of the word for struggling to grasp is lost

parts.note: gropes means struggles to understand, as in gropes for an answer

explanation.surface: Someone battles to understand, lacking the basics of what is taught.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the phrase 'learn the ropes', so the question mark marks it as an indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning the ropes means mastering the basic procedures of a job.

clue.text: River almost promptly dammed? Crikey!

indicators.note: dammed means the river has something blocking it inside

parts.note: the Forth is a Scottish river

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for promptly is lost

parts.note: soon means promptly

explanation.surface: A river is nearly blocked at once; goodness!
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts SOON to SOO, which is 'dammed' inside FORTH, the river of Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsooth is an archaic exclamation of surprise, like 'indeed!'

clue.text: Agricultural inventor close to remarkable material

parts.note: Jethro Tull invented the seed drill in the 18th century

indicators.note: close to takes the closing letter of remarkable

explanation.surface: A farming innovator near a remarkable fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Jethro Tull was an English farmer who invented the horse-drawn seed drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulle is a fine silk netting used for veils.

clue.text: At work and in peak position

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Busy and at the top of one's game.
explanation.definitionFit: Atop means on top of something, at its summit.

clue.text: Erect place -originally it's designed for holding operation

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Erect place -originally it's designed for holding operation' (10). ERECT PLACE alone anagrams to the answer, leaving both 'originally' and 'operation' with no job; no parse uses every word and no source gives the printed clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: Erect place -originally it's designed for holding operation

clue.text: She's 25,working in cafes

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are set to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: 25 refers to the answer of clue 25 across, meaning on top

explanation.surface: A woman at work in coffee shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges SHES with ATOP, the answer to 25 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Cafés serving tea and light meals are small tearooms.

clue.text: German person following eating regime

explanation.surface: A German slimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieter is a common German man's name; also a slimmer who follows a restricted meal plan.
